title: Canonical relative exponential of a root line
statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $r\geq0$. An $A$-group scheme means a scheme over $X$ with multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying associativity, unit and inverse diagrams, as in [def-sc-group-scheme] with this base in place of a field. Put $T=\mathbf G_{m,A}^r=\operatorname{Spec}A[M]$, $M=\mathbf Z^r$, where $A[M]=A[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$, $e^m=\prod_jz_j^{m_j}$, and the group law is multiplication of units. Write $\chi_m:T\to\mathbf G_{m,A}$ for the character $e^m$. Let $G$ be a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] affine finite-type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] $A$-group scheme with a closed inclusion $T\hookrightarrow G$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Assume every geometric fibre of $G$ is reductive, meaning connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent closed subgroup. Unipotent means that all geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful representation. Assume $T$ is a maximal torus in every geometric fibre, where a torus over an algebraically closed field is a product of multiplicative groups and maximality is for subgroup inclusion. Put $\mathfrak g=\ker(G(A[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))\to G(A))$, with addition induced by multiplication in $G$ and scalar multiplication induced by $\epsilon\mapsto a\epsilon$. The conjugation coaction of $T$ on this tangent module is denoted $\rho$, and $\mathfrak g_m=\{v:\rho(v)=v\otimes e^m\}$. For any $\alpha\in M\setminus\{0\}$ such that $\mathfrak g_\alpha$ is locally free of rank one on $X$, put $V_\alpha=\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{Sym}_A(\operatorname{Hom}_A(\mathfrak g_\alpha,A))$, with addition; its $B$-points are $B\otimes_A\mathfrak g_\alpha$. There is a unique $T$-equivariant group homomorphism $\exp_\alpha:V_\alpha\to G$ whose tangent map is the inclusion $\mathfrak g_\alpha\hookrightarrow\mathfrak g$, where $t\in T(B)$ acts on $V_\alpha(B)$ by multiplication by $\chi_\alpha(t)$. It is a closed immersion. Its image is smooth with geometrically connected fibres, and over every algebraically closed $A$-field its image is the $\alpha$-root subgroup in [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations]. The homomorphism and its closed image commute with every base change $A\to B$, including successive base changes; uniqueness holds after every such base change. No global basis of $\mathfrak g_\alpha$ is assumed.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Theorem 4.1.4, printed p.110, and its proof, pp.116-118; Remark 4.2.4. Closed canonical exponential of the root line, uniqueness and arbitrary base change. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf.

proof.text: Smoothness supplies local finite presentation; since $G$ is affine of finite type over the affine base, it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, hence of finite presentation. By [lem-sfb-relative-tangent-weight-base-change], the root line $L=\mathfrak g_\alpha$ and its coaction commute with every base change. In particular $\alpha$ is a root on each geometric fibre. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-root-rank-one-centralizer] to obtain $H=Z_G(T_\alpha)$ with tangent module $\mathfrak t\oplus L\oplus\mathfrak g_{-\alpha}$. Any possible $T$-equivariant homomorphism $V_\alpha\to G$ factors through $H$: $T_\alpha$ acts trivially on its source, so its image commutes with $T_\alpha$ after every algebra extension, precisely the centralizer's defining condition. This factorization remains valid over every $A$-algebra.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.4 proof, printed p.116, first paragraph; Lemma 4.1.3.

proof.text: Choose $\lambda\in\operatorname{Hom}(M,\mathbf Z)$ with $n=\lambda(\alpha)>0$: choose a nonzero coordinate of $\alpha$ and give the corresponding coordinate projection its sign. Use conjugation through $\lambda:\mathbf G_m\to T\subseteq H$. Its tangent weights on $H$ are $0,n,-n$. By [lem-sfb-relative-dynamic-attracting-subgroup] the contracting subgroup $U\subseteq H$ is smooth affine finitely presented with geometrically connected unipotent fibres and tangent module exactly $L$. It is $T$-stable: the orbit of $tut^{-1}$ is $t\lambda(c)u\lambda(c)^{-1}t^{-1}$, whose extension at zero is $1$. On each geometric fibre $U$ is therefore the root subgroup by [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations], so it is isomorphic to $\mathbf G_a$. The same dynamic theorem gives the contraction of $U$ inside itself.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.4 proof, printed pp.116-117, positive-weight subgroup; Theorem 4.1.7.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-contracted-smooth-curve-linearization] to $U$ with weight $n$. On each affine etale chart $S_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ it supplies a scaling-equivariant group isomorphism $q_i:\mathbf G_a\to U_{S_i}$. Its derivative is a basis $v_i=dq_i(1)$ of $L_i$. Define $e_i:V(L_i)\to U_{S_i}$ by $e_i(bv_i)=q_i(b)$. This is a group isomorphism equivariant for $c\cdot v=c^nv$, and its derivative is the identity of $L_i$. This construction uses each chart's basis only temporarily.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.4 proof, printed pp.117-118, normalization after Lemma 4.2.2.

proof.text: For any ring $R$ and $n>0$, a morphism $f:\mathbf A^1_R\to\mathbf A^1_R$ equivariant for $c\cdot x=c^nx$ is a polynomial $\sum a_jx^j$ satisfying $\sum a_jc^{nj}x^j=\sum a_jc^nx^j$ in $R[c,c^{-1},x]$. Independence of Laurent monomials implies $a_j=0$ for $j\ne1$; hence $f(x)=a_1x$. This works over nonreduced rings and when $n$ is not a unit. In the coordinates of Step 3 it shows that a scaling-equivariant map of these line groups is uniquely determined by its tangent map. On every overlap $e_j^{-1}e_i$ has tangent identity and is scaling-equivariant, so it is the identity. For the universal $t\in T$ over $S_i\times_ST$, conjugation by $t$ on $U$ commutes with $\lambda$ and has derivative multiplication by $\chi_\alpha(t)$. The same polynomial calculation therefore gives $t e_i(v)t^{-1}=e_i(\chi_\alpha(t)v)$. Thus the $e_i$ are $T$-equivariant, as maps of schemes, rather than merely on residue-field points.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.4 proof, printed p.117, equivariant polynomial calculation; agent expansion of full torus equivariance.

proof.text: The etale covering is fpqc by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale]; its pullbacks to $V_\alpha$, $U$, their products and their torus products are fpqc by [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] to the compatible maps $e_i$ and separately to $e_i^{-1}$. It gives inverse global maps $e:V_\alpha\simeq U$; equality after these covers proves that they are inverses. Checking multiplication, identity, $T$-equivariance and the tangent inclusion on the same covers gives all the asserted identities. Compose $e$ with the closed subgroup inclusions $U\hookrightarrow H\hookrightarrow G$ to define $\exp_\alpha$. Its closed image is $U$; smoothness, geometric connectedness and the geometric root-subgroup identification were established in Step 2.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.4 proof, printed pp.116-118, etale-local argument and descent; Stacks Tag 023Q, lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms.

proof.text: Let $f:V_\alpha\to G$ be any $T$-equivariant group homomorphism with the prescribed derivative. Step 1 factors it through $H$. Each source point $v$ has contracting orbit $c\mapsto c^nv$ with value zero at zero. Equivariant functoriality in [lem-sfb-relative-dynamic-attracting-subgroup] therefore factors $f$ through $U$. On each chart of Step 3, $e_i^{-1}f$ is a scaling-equivariant endomorphism of the additive line with tangent identity. Step 4 makes it the identity. Uniqueness of morphism descent in [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent], on the pulled-back fpqc cover of Step 5, implies $f=\exp_\alpha$. This proves uniqueness among all the stated homomorphisms, without assuming in advance that $f$ is an immersion.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.4 proof, printed pp.116-117, factorization through the contracting subgroup and uniqueness.

proof.text: For an arbitrary $A$-algebra $B$, including nonflat and non-Noetherian ones, [lem-sfb-relative-tangent-weight-base-change] identifies the source after base change with the additive group of $B\otimes_A L$ and identifies its derivative. The centralizer and dynamic subgroup identifications in [lem-sfb-relative-root-rank-one-centralizer] and [lem-sfb-relative-dynamic-attracting-subgroup] identify $H_B,U_B$ with the corresponding functors over $B$. The maps $e_i$ and their inverses pull back to an etale cover of $\operatorname{Spec}B$, so Steps 4 and 6 apply over $B$ verbatim: their only ring calculation is equality of Laurent-polynomial coefficients. The pullback of $\exp_\alpha$ is therefore the unique map with the required derivative and equivariance over $B$, with closed image $U_B$. For $A\to B\to C$, both constructions over $C$ have these properties and hence agree. If $B$ is the zero ring all schemes concerned are empty over its spectrum and the assertions hold uniquely.
